items.title: 'Even sleep is expensive': The challenge for a people forced to live in ruins
items.description: It's been seven months since the ceasefire in Gaza, but reconstruction has barely begun, water remains contaminated and minimal aid is getting into the strip. This is what life is like for its residents.

items.title: The housing 'super cycle' may be ending, and that could be a good thing
items.description: Before the federal budget, the housing market was already starting to choke on its own excesses. Now some economists are tipping an extended period where home prices grow no faster than general inflation.

items.title: 'Perverse logic' over abortion, Barnaby Joyce tells Sydney crowd
items.description: Nine months out from the NSW election campaign, One Nation recruit Barnaby Joyce has appeared in Sydney, declaring politicians are fearful of losing their jobs.

items.title: Snowy 2.0 blows out by more than $3m a day. Will it ever be worth it?
items.description: Australia's most ambitious renewable energy project is slowly nearing completion, but experts are divided on whether Snowy 2.0 will ever justify its snowballing price tag.

items.title: Australian men guilty after taking 'black flight' to flee country
items.description: Three Australian men have been found guilty by a District Court in Merauke after taking a "black flight" into Indonesia's South Papua province from Far North Queensland without visas.

items.title: Trump drops $2.5b 'weaponization' fund plans amid corruption allegations
items.description: The US president has abandoned plans for a $2.51 billion "anti-weaponization" fund for ‌victims of alleged government "weaponization", according to the acting attorney-general.

items.title: Trump names inexperienced ally as intelligence director
items.description: Bill Pulte, who is known for publicly attacking the US president's political enemies, would also retain his existing jobs overseeing federal housing and mortgage policies.

items.title: Live: Marles says Australia wanted three second-hand subs all along
items.description: The defence minister says the new AUKUS deal that will see Australia buy three second-hand Virginia-class submarines from the US is what the government had wanted all along. Follow live.

items.title: UK PM calls video of handcuffed dying teen 'harrowing' amid protests
items.description: The British prime minister says he "felt sick" while watching a video released by police of 18-year-old Henry Nowak, who was handcuffed while he lay dying from stab wounds after his killer falsely alleged a racist attack.

items.title: Former Canberra Liberals leader leaves party citing 'toxic culture'
items.description: Former Canberra Liberals Leanne Castley has resigned from the Canberra Liberals, saying she "can no longer be part of an organisation ... with such a toxic culture".

items.title: Live: Oil prices rise on US-Iran uncertainty, ASX to open higher with AI stocks at record highs
items.description: Oil prices jump to a one-week high as the US and Iran provide conflicting updates on their peace talks. The Australian share market is likely to start higher after a surge in AI stocks on Wall Street overnight. Follow live.

items.title: Enormous ship en route to pick up world's largest electric ferry
items.description: The 217-metre-long heavy-lift vessel Black Marlin will deliver a Tasmanian shipbuilder's new electric ferry to South America, after the previous transporter became caught up in the Strait of Hormuz closure.

items.title: These companies have controversial pasts. Google AI didn't tell us
items.description: We searched Google for information on some of the world's biggest tobacco companies. The results raised questions about how much of the AI overview was coming from the brands themselves.

items.title: 'Flat-pack' homes hoped to save country towns from 'domino effect'
items.description: A Queensland outback town pins its hopes of solving a local housing crisis on "flat-pack" homes as the high cost of building risks paralysing the community.

items.title: Why Hugh Jackman's brother cried on his first day as a prison-school teacher
items.description: After Ralph Jackman retrained as a teacher, his first job was in a youth detention centre. His new memoir reveals how a broken system is failing vulnerable kids.

items.title: This rapper was having panic attacks on stage, until he transitioned
items.description: Poet, rapper, musician, playwright and novelist Kae Tempest is a prodigious polymath. It wasn't until he affirmed his gender that he connected with his true self.

items.title: Quiz: Hold on to your hat, we're off on a tour of the globe
items.description: The famous US road trip along Route 66 links which two cities? And which country eats the most garlic per person?

items.title: Deadly heatwave 'tip of the iceberg' in India as UN sends El Niño warning
items.description: India's deadly heatwave comes as the UN warns the world to prepare for a moderate to strong El Niño this year.

items.title: Rocket motor test success marks Australian-made missile milestone
items.description: In what is being described as a significant leap forward in Australia's push to develop and manufacture its own missiles, newly released footage shows the first test-firing of a locally made solid rocket motor.

items.title: Government says it preferred second-hand submarines
items.description: Australia and the United States' initial positions about delivering a new submarine under AUKUS differed, Senate estimates has revealed.

items.title: Major Russian attack on Ukraine leaves at least 22 dead and dozens injured
items.description: Moscow targeted Kyiv and other cities, killing multiple people, damaging buildings and leaving wounded trapped under rubble, local authorities say.

items.title: Premier tells member to take complaint to body which doesn't exist yet
items.description: Jeremy Rockliff won't investigate how an email containing the health-related information of a politician was leaked to the media and suggests she could take up the matter with a complaints body that doesn't exist yet.

items.title: Black market adapts after Qld's illicit tobacco and vape shop crackdown
items.description: Queensland's crackdown has reduced visible illicit tobacco sales, according to a public health researcher, but the black market has adapted, prompting calls for the tobacco excise to be cut.

items.title: Semaglutide is used for weight loss but may benefit kidneys and heart
items.description: Research shows semaglutide — commonly sold as Ozempic or Wegovy — can improve kidney function and survival rates for people with some chronic diseases, even if they have heart issues.

items.title: Emotional Ukrainian star not accepting silence from Russian players
items.description: Ukrainian star Marta Kostyuk says it is unacceptable for Russians to stay silent on the war, especially after Daria Kasatkina's defection to Australia.
